title: FA reviewing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s UK ‘colonised by immigrants’ comments
content:
The Football Association (FA) is looking into comments made by Sir Jim Ratcliffe after the Manchester United co-owner claimed that Britain has been “colonised by immigrants”.

During an interview with Sky News on Wednesday, Ratcliffe, a British billionaire who has resided in Monaco — a tax haven — since 2020, made multiple inflammatory and inaccurate observations about the United Kingdom’s immigrant population.

After making the comments, which were widely condemned by politicians and fans of Manchester United, FA sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, indicated that although the governing body is yet to launch a formal investigation, it is now reviewing Ratcliffe’s remarks to see if there is a rule breach.

“You can’t have an economy with nine million people on benefits and huge levels of immigrants coming in,” Ratcliffe said.

“I mean, the UK has been colonised. It’s costing too much money. The UK has been colonised by immigrants, really, hasn’t it? I mean, the population of the UK was 58 million in 2020, now it’s 70 million. That’s 12 million people.”

The UK’s Office for National Statistics estimated that the UK population was 69.5 million in November 2025, compared to 67.1 million in 2020. The ONS also estimated that the UK’s long-term net migration was 204,000 from 2024 to 2025.

According to a House of Commons research briefing from January there were 1.68 million people, as of December 2025, claiming unemployment-related benefits in the UK.

Under FA Rule E3.1, which covers general behaviour, the governing body of English football outlines that “participants” must act in the best interests of the game and avoid improper or disreputable conduct.

This can include the use violent, threading, indecent, or insulting language, and Ratcliffe, as a director at Manchester United, would be categorised as a “participant” in this context.

A breach of Rule E3.1 is considered an “aggravated breach” when it includes a reference, whether express or implied, to: ethnic origin, colour, race, nationality, religion or belief, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation or disability.

Ratcliffe also said the UK needs a prime minister who is “prepared to be unpopular … to get the big issues sorted”, comparing that role to his own at United, where he has been “very unpopular” because of the changes made since his arrival in 2024.

Sir Keir Starmer, the UK’s prime minister, responded to Ratcliffe’s comments via a post on X, describing them as “offensive and wrong”. Starmer also called on the United co-owner to apologise.

Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham said the comments “go against everything for which Manchester has traditionally stood: a place where people of all races, faiths and none have pulled together over centuries to build our city and our institutions, including Manchester United FC”.
